passages.text: Peter said, “If this is so, you act with the greatest impiety. For if it belongs to the Son who ordered heaven and earth to reveal his Father in secrecy to whomever he wishes, you, as I said, act with the greatest impiety by revealing to those to whom he did not reveal.” Simon said, “But he himself wants me to reveal.” Peter said, “You do not understand what I say, Simon. Yet listen and understand. Saying, ‘To those to whom the Son wishes he will reveal,’ does not mean that someone learns such a thing by teaching, but only by revelation. Revelation is what lies secretly in all human hearts, covered, being uncovered without a voice by his will. Thus one comes to know not by being taught, but by understanding. Yet the one who has understood is not permitted to demonstrate this to another, since he himself was not taught; nor can he reveal it, since he himself is not the Son—unless he says that he himself is the Son. But you are not the standing Son. For if you were Son, you would certainly know those worthy of such revelation. But you do not know. For if you knew, you would do the things done by those who know.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἄνευ φωνῆς τῆς αὐτοῦ βουλῆς ἀποκαλυπτόμενον
lexical_decisions.chosen: being uncovered without a voice by his will
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase can be grouped as without a voice, by his will, or without a voice expressing his will. The main rendering keeps the nonvocal disclosure and its relation to his will without adding spoken instruction.
Keeps the standing epithet and Son together, rather than replacing them with a later named title or deleting the unusual description.

passages.text: Simon said, “I admit I did not understand how you mean, ‘You would do the things done by those who know.’” Peter said, “If you did not understand, you also cannot know each person’s mind. And if you do not know, you also do not know those worthy of revelation. If you do not know, you are not Son; but the Son knows, and therefore reveals to those he wishes as being worthy.” Simon said, “Do not deceive: I know those who are worthy, and I am not Son. Yet I did not understand what this is, ‘He reveals to those he wishes,’ as you say. I said that I did not understand not because I did not know, but because I knew that those present did not understand, so that you would state it more clearly and those for whose sake we also conduct the discussion might understand.” Peter said, “I cannot state it more clearly. Since you have understood it, explain it yourself.” Simon said, “I am not obliged to state your views.” Peter said, “It seems to me, Simon, that you do not understand it and are unwilling to admit it, lest, being caught in ignorance, you be exposed as not being the standing Son. For this is what you hint at, even if you do not wish to say it plainly. Thus I know your intentions from your hints, being a disciple of a true prophet, not a prophet. But you, though you do not understand even what is plainly said, wish to call yourself Son, standing against us.” Simon said, “I will remove every excuse from you. I admit that I did not understand what this is: ‘And to those to whom the Son wishes, he reveals.’ So state it more clearly.”

lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the epithet tied to Simon’s alleged claim; it is not identified with an external historical person.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: προφήτου ἀληθοῦς μαθητὴς ὤν, οὐ προφήτης
lexical_decisions.chosen: being a disciple of a true prophet, not a prophet
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves Peter’s explicit denial of being a prophet in this statement, rather than harmonizing it to a later title.

passages.text: Peter said, “Since you have admitted, even if only for appearances, that you do not understand it, answer what I ask you, and you will learn. Tell me: do you say that the Son, whoever he may be, is just, or not?” Simon said, “Most just.” Peter said, “If he is just, why does he not reveal to all, but to those he wishes?” Simon said, “Because, being just, he wishes to reveal to those who are worthy.” Peter said, “Then must he not know each person’s mind so that he may reveal to the worthy?” Simon said, “It must certainly be so.” Peter said, “Then he alone was reasonably appointed to reveal, since he alone knows each person’s mind—not you, who cannot even understand the things we say.”

lexical_decisions.rationale: σχήματι can indicate outward form or pretense; even formally is a less interpretive alternative. The admission is treated skeptically, not accepted as sincere without qualification.

passages.text: After Peter said this, praise arose from the crowds. Simon, thoroughly exposed, blushed in shame, rubbed his forehead, and said, “But they call me a magician, defeated by Peter, and also caught in argument. Yet if someone is caught in argument and taken unawares, he does not thereby have the truth within him defeated; for the weakness of its defender is not the truth of the defeated party. Nevertheless I tell you that I judged everyone present worthy to know the Father in secrecy. Therefore, when I reveal him to them publicly, they should not be angry with me out of envy, since I wish to do them good.”

lexical_decisions.rationale: The form can mean reasoning or being brought under a syllogistic argument. The context of defeat and being taken unawares favors being caught in argument; reasoning is a material alternative.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐ γὰρ ἡ ἀσθένεια τοῦ ἐκδικοῦντος ἀλήθειά ἐστιν τοῦ νικωμένου
lexical_decisions.chosen: the weakness of its defender is not the truth of the defeated party
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the compact distinction between a weak defender and the truth he defends rather than rewriting it as truth’s weakness.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐ αὐτοῖς διὰ φθόνον ἐμοὶ τῷ εὐεργετεῖν αὐτοὺς θέλοντι χαλεπαίνειν
lexical_decisions.chosen: they should not be angry with me out of envy, since I wish to do them good
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes αὐτοῖς as the persons for whom getting angry is inappropriate, leaving the grammatical third-person reference intact instead of silently changing it to you, Peter.

passages.text: Peter said, “Since you have spoken in this way to please the crowds present, I will speak not to please them, but truthfully. Tell me: how do you know that everyone present is worthy, when not even one agreed with you as you disclosed it? For their praising me against you is not the act of people agreeing with you, but with me, to whom they also assigned praise as someone who had spoken rightly. But since God, being just, judges each person’s mind—which you say is true—he would not have wished this to be given to those on the right through the left. By the same reasoning, someone who receives anything from a thief is himself liable. Therefore, for this reason, he did not wish them to receive what you bring, but rather through the Son appointed to reveal. For to whom is it reasonable to reveal the Father, except the Son alone, because he knows the person worthy of such revelation? Thus this cannot be taught or learned by teaching, but must be revealed by an inexpressible hand to the one worthy to know it.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: to those on the right through the left
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the right/left opposition without identifying unprinted named camps or persons.
Retains the hand image, not merely a generic divine act.
